Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On June 26, 2024, the United States, Japan, and South Korea held their inaugural trilateral Commerce and Industry Ministerial Meeting in Washington, D.C., establishing a framework to enhance cooperation on economic security and supply chain resilience. [4, 6] The agreement specifically aims to bolster refining and processing capabilities for critical minerals, including gallium, germanium, and graphite, to reduce dependence on other suppliers. [8] The ministers, U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo, Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade, and Industry Ken Saito, and Republic of Korea Minister of Trade, Industry, and Energy Ahn Duk-geun, committed to annual meetings to continue collaboration on key technology sectors such as semiconductors, batteries, and artificial intelligence. [4, 6] <2> A market report published on May 21, 2024, projected that the global revenue from gallium sales will increase from $2.45 billion in 2024 to $21.53 billion by the end of 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.3%. The report anticipates the United States market to reach a value of $247.8 million in 2024. Surging prices for the metal are encouraging companies to find new supply sources to meet the expanding demand, which is driven by its use in semiconductors for electronics like smartphones and computers, as well as in the growing solar industry. <3> A market report focusing on 2024 projects that the United States will hold a dominant 79.6% revenue share of the North American gallium market. This significant market position is attributed to strong demand from several key industries, including the electronics, defense, aerospace, healthcare, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sectors. Further growth in the U.S. market is anticipated, bolstered by the strategically important discovery of a high-grade gallium deposit in March 2024. The discovery was made by US Critical Materials within its 6,700-acre claims in Sheep Creek, Montana. <4> A report published on April 3, 2024, highlighted that international prices for gallium had more than doubled since China implemented export restrictions in 2023. [3] By the end of March 2024, the price for gallium metal delivered to Rotterdam reached $575 per kilogram. [3] The price increase is a direct consequence of China, which refines approximately 94% of the world's gallium, placing the metal under stricter government oversight and licensing requirements, significantly crimping global supply. [3] <5> On March 21, 2024, US Critical Materials Corp. announced the confirmation of a 'strategically significant' high-grade gallium deposit on its 6,700 acres of claims at the Sheep Creek property in Montana. This discovery is critical for the United States, which is currently 100% dependent on imported gallium, primarily from China. The situation has been heightened by recent export restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on gallium, a material vital for national defense, semiconductors, 5G technology, and satellite systems. <6> Efficient Power Conversion Corporation (EPC) announced the launch of the EPC2361, a 100V Gallium Nitride (GaN) Field-Effect Transistor (FET) with an on-resistance of 1 mΩ, at the APEC 2024 conference. [8] EPC claims this is the lowest on-resistance GaN FET currently on the market, offering double the power density of its previous generation products. [4] Housed in a compact 3 mm x 5 mm QFN package, the EPC2361 is designed to improve efficiency and power density in a variety of applications. [4] These include high-frequency DC-DC conversion for data centers, AC-DC synchronous rectification for power supplies, motor drives for eMobility, robotics, and drones, as well as solar MPPT and fast charging systems. [4] <7> On February 19, 2024, the U.S. Department of Commerce announced a non-binding preliminary memorandum of terms to provide GlobalFoundries with approximately $1.5 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. [4, 5] A portion of this investment is designated for modernizing its facility in Essex Junction, Vermont, to create the first U.S. facility capable of high-volume manufacturing of next-generation Gallium Nitride (GaN) on Silicon semiconductors. [4] These chips are crucial for a variety of technologies, including electric vehicles, power grids, 5G and 6G smartphones, data centers, and other critical aerospace and defense applications. [4] The proposed funding is part of a larger investment to expand GlobalFoundries' U.S. manufacturing, which also includes the construction of a new fab and the expansion of an existing one in Malta, New York. [4, 5] <8> A report from IMARC Group, published on January 1, 2024, stated that the price of gallium in China reached $415,169 per metric ton during December 2023. [2] This price point was influenced by China's export controls, which have a significant impact on the global gallium market as China is the world's primary producer. [2, 3, 5] These trade regulations and geopolitical factors have historically led to price volatility and prompted manufacturers in regions like North America and Europe to seek more stable supply chains. [2, 3] <9> In its 2024 outlook, Deloitte forecast that multiple regions, including the United States, could face shortages of gallium. This prediction was attributed to the continued stringent implementation of China's export controls, which persisted through the end of 2023. The controls were expected to keep impacting supply chains and the availability of the metal. The situation was compounded by reports of low non-Chinese gallium stocks and an inability of limited production outside China to meet consumption demands, leading to the characterization of 2024 as a potentially decisive year for the gallium market outside of China. <10> On December 15, 2023, Fastmarkets assessed the price for gallium 99.99% Ga min, in-warehouse Rotterdam, at $500-600 per kg, a 9% increase from the $460-550 per kg price recorded at the start of the month. This price surge in the European market, a key indicator for US pricing, was attributed to a tightening supply as non-Chinese stocks were reportedly diminishing. The situation was further compounded by Japanese consumers outbidding European buyers for the limited available inventory, all of which was exacerbated by China's persistent and stringent export controls on the metal.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) released its annual "State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry" report, which found that since the introduction of the CHIPS Act, companies have announced over 90 new manufacturing projects in the U.S. totaling nearly $450 billion in investments across 28 states as of August 2024. The report's release coincided with a forecast from the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization, endorsed by the SIA, projecting global semiconductor sales will increase by 16% in 2024 to a record $611.2 billion. <2> On June 26, 2024, the United States, Japan, and South Korea held their inaugural trilateral Commerce and Industry Ministerial Meeting in Washington, D.C., establishing a framework to enhance cooperation on economic security and supply chain resilience. [4, 6] The agreement specifically aims to bolster refining and processing capabilities for critical minerals, including gallium, germanium, and graphite, to reduce dependence on other suppliers. [8] The ministers, U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo, Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade, and Industry Ken Saito, and Republic of Korea Minister of Trade, Industry, and Energy Ahn Duk-geun, committed to annual meetings to continue collaboration on key technology sectors such as semiconductors, batteries, and artificial intelligence. [4, 6] <3> A market report published on May 21, 2024, projected that the global revenue from gallium sales will increase from $2.45 billion in 2024 to $21.53 billion by the end of 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.3%. The report anticipates the United States market to reach a value of $247.8 million in 2024. Surging prices for the metal are encouraging companies to find new supply sources to meet the expanding demand, which is driven by its use in semiconductors for electronics like smartphones and computers, as well as in the growing solar industry. <4> A market report focusing on 2024 projects that the United States will hold a dominant 79.6% revenue share of the North American gallium market. This significant market position is attributed to strong demand from several key industries, including the electronics, defense, aerospace, healthcare, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sectors. Further growth in the U.S. market is anticipated, bolstered by the strategically important discovery of a high-grade gallium deposit in March 2024. The discovery was made by US Critical Materials within its 6,700-acre claims in Sheep Creek, Montana. <5> A report published on April 3, 2024, highlighted that international prices for gallium had more than doubled since China implemented export restrictions in 2023. [3] By the end of March 2024, the price for gallium metal delivered to Rotterdam reached $575 per kilogram. [3] The price increase is a direct consequence of China, which refines approximately 94% of the world's gallium, placing the metal under stricter government oversight and licensing requirements, significantly crimping global supply. [3] <6> On March 21, 2024, US Critical Materials Corp. announced the confirmation of a 'strategically significant' high-grade gallium deposit on its 6,700 acres of claims at the Sheep Creek property in Montana. This discovery is critical for the United States, which is currently 100% dependent on imported gallium, primarily from China. The situation has been heightened by recent export restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on gallium, a material vital for national defense, semiconductors, 5G technology, and satellite systems. <7> Efficient Power Conversion Corporation (EPC) announced the launch of the EPC2361, a 100V Gallium Nitride (GaN) Field-Effect Transistor (FET) with an on-resistance of 1 mΩ, at the APEC 2024 conference. [8] EPC claims this is the lowest on-resistance GaN FET currently on the market, offering double the power density of its previous generation products. [4] Housed in a compact 3 mm x 5 mm QFN package, the EPC2361 is designed to improve efficiency and power density in a variety of applications. [4] These include high-frequency DC-DC conversion for data centers, AC-DC synchronous rectification for power supplies, motor drives for eMobility, robotics, and drones, as well as solar MPPT and fast charging systems. [4] <8> On February 19, 2024, the U.S. Department of Commerce announced a non-binding preliminary memorandum of terms to provide GlobalFoundries with approximately $1.5 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. [4, 5] A portion of this investment is designated for modernizing its facility in Essex Junction, Vermont, to create the first U.S. facility capable of high-volume manufacturing of next-generation Gallium Nitride (GaN) on Silicon semiconductors. [4] These chips are crucial for a variety of technologies, including electric vehicles, power grids, 5G and 6G smartphones, data centers, and other critical aerospace and defense applications. [4] The proposed funding is part of a larger investment to expand GlobalFoundries' U.S. manufacturing, which also includes the construction of a new fab and the expansion of an existing one in Malta, New York. [4, 5] <9> A report from IMARC Group, published on January 1, 2024, stated that the price of gallium in China reached $415,169 per metric ton during December 2023. [2] This price point was influenced by China's export controls, which have a significant impact on the global gallium market as China is the world's primary producer. [2, 3, 5] These trade regulations and geopolitical factors have historically led to price volatility and prompted manufacturers in regions like North America and Europe to seek more stable supply chains. [2, 3] <10> In its 2024 outlook, Deloitte forecast that multiple regions, including the United States, could face shortages of gallium. This prediction was attributed to the continued stringent implementation of China's export controls, which persisted through the end of 2023. The controls were expected to keep impacting supply chains and the availability of the metal. The situation was compounded by reports of low non-Chinese gallium stocks and an inability of limited production outside China to meet consumption demands, leading to the characterization of 2024 as a potentially decisive year for the gallium market outside of China.

metadata.original_text: This time series records gallium CNY Kg data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-03-14 to 2025-03-31. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A market outlook report from Persistence Market Research forecasts significant growth for the global gallium market, projecting an increase from US$ 3.7 billion in 2025 to US$ 17.0 billion by 2032, at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.5%. [2] The report identifies China's export controls, initiated in August 2023, as a major factor influencing global supply dynamics and heightening concerns about supply security. [2] Consequently, these restrictions have spurred new initiatives in the United States, Europe, and Japan to develop domestic production capabilities. A notable development in the U.S. is the Geological Survey's discovery of high-grade gallium deposits in Montana, which is seen as a critical move toward reducing reliance on imports. [2] <2> MTM Critical Metals (ASX:MTM) announced it is finalizing the design of a one-ton-per-day modular pilot plant that utilizes Flash Joule Heating (FJH) technology to recover critical metals. The company anticipated the completion of the process and mechanical design criteria by the end of February 2025. This demonstration plant is a key milestone in the company's strategy to commercialize its technology, with the plant's startup targeted for the fourth quarter of 2025. MTM aims to achieve commercial production and generate cash flow in 2025, focusing on re-shoring the production of strategic metals like gallium, germanium, and rare earth elements in the United States from various feedstocks, including manufacturing and electronic waste. <3> On January 20, 2025, the first day of his new administration, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14156, declaring a National Energy Emergency. [1, 5, 6] The order stated that the United States' capacity for energy and critical minerals identification, development, and production was "far too inadequate to meet our Nation’s needs." [1, 2] This inadequacy was cited as an "unusual and extraordinary threat" to the nation's economy and security. [1] The executive order broadly defined "energy resources" to include critical minerals alongside fossil fuels like crude oil and natural gas, but it did not specifically name gallium. [2, 7] The order directed federal agencies to use all available emergency authorities to expedite the development of domestic energy resources. [5, 7] <4> Greenwave Technology Solutions announced it is fast-tracking its rare-earth metal recovery initiatives; including gallium from solar cells and electronic waste; in response to China's ban on exporting these materials to the United States <5> A market research report by Allied Market Research analyzed key trends that shaped the semiconductor and electronics sector in the fourth quarter of 2024. The report highlighted a growing demand for power electronic components, noting that the development of wide-bandgap semiconductors like gallium nitride (GaN) has led to significant advancements in the power electronics industry. Additional key trends included advancements in 3D IC, with the rise of 3D packaging technology fueling market growth. The report also pointed to growth in advanced packaging, driven by factors such as the medical industry's demand for nano-sized robotic surgery equipment and the rapid evolution of wearable and personalized devices. <6> The event escalated in two key phases. Initially, on July 3, 2023, China's Ministry of Commerce announced that export licenses would be required for gallium and germanium products, a measure that took effect on August 1, 2023. [5, 6, 7, 17] This initial step was not a ban and applied globally, but was widely viewed as a response to U.S. restrictions on semiconductor technology. [15, 16] The more significant escalation occurred on December 3, 2024, when Beijing explicitly banned the export of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the United States. [3, 4, 10] This outright ban was a direct retaliation, announced a day after Washington expanded its own controls on chip-making equipment sales to China. [4, 11, 13] The targeted minerals are critical for manufacturing semiconductors, defense technologies, and electric vehicles, and the ban represents a major escalation in the ongoing trade and technology rivalry between the two countries. [12] <7> In response to China's expanding export restrictions on critical minerals, United States allies and partners are intensifying efforts to secure their own supply chains. The urgency of these initiatives was underscored by China's Ministry of Commerce announcing an immediate ban on the export of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the U.S. on December 3, 2024, citing national security interests. [3, 4, 5, 6] These minerals are essential for semiconductors, defense technologies, and other next-generation applications. [2] This move has prompted nations like Australia, India, Japan, and South Korea, particularly through collaborative efforts like the Quad's Critical Minerals Partnership, to develop alternative sources and mitigate the risks of overdependence on Chinese supplies. [7] <8> A U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) study, released in a national news brief on November 19, 2024, modeled the potential economic repercussions of a complete Chinese embargo on gallium and germanium exports. [7] The research, titled “Quantifying Potential Effects of China’s Gallium and Germanium Export Restrictions,” estimated that a total ban could lead to a $3.4 billion decrease in the U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP). [2, 7] The study highlighted the particular vulnerability of the U.S. semiconductor industry, which would bear over 40% of the net economic losses. [5, 7] In such a scenario, the model predicted that gallium prices could surge by over 150%, while germanium prices could rise by 26%. [5, 7] This analysis was prompted by China's 2023 implementation of export licensing controls on these critical minerals, which are vital for semiconductors and other high-tech manufacturing. [3, 7] <9> On November 15, 2024, the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Critical Materials Innovation Hub (CMI Hub) announced up to $10 million in federal funding. The funding is intended to accelerate early-stage research and development to reduce the nation's reliance on critical materials—specifically rare-earth elements, gallium, and copper—for energy innovations. The request for proposals targets several key areas, including the efficient recovery of gallium as a byproduct, the creation of new compounds to lessen the amount of gallium in semiconductors, and improved manufacturing processes to minimize waste. This initiative is part of a broader effort by the CMI Hub, which is led by the Ames Laboratory, to strengthen domestic supply chains for materials subject to price volatility and supply disruptions.
